name: Maintain hydro plants and dams (one work order)
summary: Operator-maintainers and electricians based at area shops keep seventeen mostly unstaffed hydro plants and their dams, gates and canals working. Each work order is either a preventive task released by the ERP from a maintenance plan or a repair requested by the control centre, site staff or dam safety engineers; the supervisor plans and schedules it, the crew drives to site, isolates the equipment with the control centre, does the work and records it. Larger jobs need a specialist crew from engineering and a unit outage timed to low flows. Work is slowed by weekly scheduling backlogs, parts lead times, long drives to remote sites, winter weather and the wait for specialist crews.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator with seventeen hydro plants on the Bow, North Saskatchewan and Oldman rivers run from one Calgary control centre, alongside converted gas units and wind farms.
baseline.notes: ERP plant maintenance module, paper or electronic permits, and spreadsheets for the weekly schedule, as was common in 2019-2022.

trigger: A preventive work order falls due in the ERP, or a corrective work request is submitted.
end_state: The work is done, the equipment is back in service and the work order is closed with hours and failure codes, or the request is cancelled.

volume.seasonality: Preventive and outage work concentrates in the autumn and winter low-flow months; spring runoff limits unit outages from May to July.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate (about 32 orders per plant per month including routine site checks), kept because no public figure was found.

surge.cause: repairs after a high-flow event (debris, intake, gate and erosion damage)

evidence.note: Estimate; high-flow events on the Bow occur in June.
Most of the 42 operator-maintainers' time goes to work orders; the rest to callouts, surveillance rounds and training.
Most of the 14 electricians' time; estimate.
Planning, scheduling and closing orders across six supervisors; estimate.
Switching for planned work; estimate.
Specialist crew lead time on hydro jobs; estimate.

systems.name: ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)
Document management and engineering drawings repository
Outage and project scheduling software (critical path)
Hydro, wind and battery SCADA and remote control

resources.name: Hydro plant with dam and reservoir

steps.name: ERP issues preventive order or logs request
steps.description: The ERP plant maintenance module releases preventive work orders from the maintenance plans when they fall due (inspections, lubrication, gate exercising, protection tests), and records corrective work requests raised by operators, operator-maintainers or the dam safety engineers.

next.condition: preventive order from a maintenance plan

evidence.note: Preventive work follows approved schedules and manufacturer guidance (s11); the preventive share is an estimate.

steps.name: Screen corrective request
steps.description: The hydro operations supervisor reads the request, checks for duplicates and recent work on the same equipment, and judges how urgent it is from the effect on the unit, the dam or safety.

error.defect_description: Priority set too low for a developing fault.

next.condition: urgent: unit, gate or safety at risk

evidence.note: Screening shares estimated.

steps.name: Approve and decide resourcing
steps.description: The supervisor approves the work order, sets the priority, and decides whether the area crew can do it or whether it needs a specialist crew from engineering and a planned unit outage.

next.condition: needs specialist crew or unit outage

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Plan the job
steps.description: The supervisor writes or copies the job plan: task steps, crew size, estimated hours, parts and tools, isolation points and permits, and links any standard job plan. Preventive orders mostly reuse the standard plan.

error.defect_description: A part is missed or hours underestimated.

evidence.note: The organisation file has no hydro maintenance planner, so supervisors are assumed to plan; time estimated.

steps.name: Request specialist crew and outage window
steps.description: The supervisor sends a crew request to engineering's specialist crews, asks Hydro Scheduling and the trading desk for a unit outage in low-flow or low-price weeks, and enters the planned outage so it can be reported to the AESO.

error.defect_description: Outage window clashes with high flows.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Specialist crew confirms crew and dates
steps.description: The specialist crew lead fits the job into the crews' outage season schedule, confirms the crew, cranes and tools, and agrees the start date with the hydro supervisor, often months later in the autumn or winter low-flow season.

evidence.note: Waits reflect a few specialist crews shared with the thermal fleet; estimate.

steps.name: Check and reserve parts
steps.description: An operator-maintainer looks up the parts on the job plan in the ERP stores catalogue, reserves what is in stock at the warehouse, and raises a material request for anything that must be bought.

next.condition: parts in stock or none needed

evidence.note: Stock-out share estimated.

steps.name: Wait for parts
steps.description: The supplier ships the purchased parts to the warehouse, the storekeeper receives them and they are sent to the area shop. Special parts for older units can take weeks.

evidence.note: Lead times estimated.

steps.name: Schedule job in weekly plan
steps.description: At the weekly scheduling meeting the supervisor slots the job by due date and priority, and agrees with the control centre and Hydro Scheduling when a unit or gate can come out of service without spilling water or missing high-price hours.

evidence.note: Weekly schedule and backlog wait estimated.

steps.name: Travel to site
steps.description: The crew loads the truck at the area shop and drives to the plant or dam. One trip usually covers several work orders at the same site, so the minutes are each order's share; winter roads and storms delay trips.

evidence.note: Plants spread across three river systems (s6); trip sharing and times estimated.

steps.name: Do pre-job hazard assessment
steps.description: The crew walks the job, fills in the field-level hazard assessment for the task (water, confined spaces, working at heights, energised equipment) and holds a short tailboard before starting.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code hazard assessment requirements and the company field-level hazard assessment

evidence.note: Isolation share estimated; hazard assessment duty named from general knowledge of the OHS Code.

steps.name: Isolate equipment from control centre
steps.description: On the crew's request the control centre operator opens breakers and closes gates remotely, places SCADA tags and issues the isolation to the permit holder in the permit system.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 (isolation, verification, personal locks, group control) and the company permit-to-work procedure

evidence.note: Control centre coordinates switching and isolations with site staff (s5); Part 15 (s10).

steps.name: Verify isolation and apply personal locks
steps.description: The permit holder tests that the equipment is de-energised and gates cannot move, every worker applies a personal lock to the group lock box, and the permit is signed on.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 (isolation, verification, personal locks, group control) and the company permit-to-work procedure

evidence.note: Verify isolation, personal locks, group control (s10).

steps.name: Do the work
steps.description: The operator-maintainers carry out the inspection, lubrication, filter or seal change, gate or hoist repair, or other task on the job plan, take readings, and note any further defects they find. Minutes are person-minutes for the crew.

evidence.note: Typical hydro maintenance tasks (s11); times and shares estimated.

steps.name: Do electrical and protection work
steps.description: The hydro electrician tests protection relays, services breakers, exciters, station batteries or control wiring, and records test results against settings.

error.defect_description: Relay setting left wrong after test.

control.basis: Alberta compulsory trade certification for electricians

evidence.note: Protection testing as routine hydro work (s11); trade rule from general knowledge.

steps.name: Specialist crew does major repair
steps.description: The specialist crew lead runs the major job (wicket gates, runner or seal repair, generator work, spillway gate hoist) with turbine and rigging technicians under a group lockout, using a mobile crane where needed. Minutes are the crew lead's own hours.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 (isolation, verification, personal locks, group control) and the company permit-to-work procedure

evidence.note: Crew size and durations estimated.

steps.name: Test and return to service
steps.description: The crew runs the equipment or unit under the control centre's watch, checks readings, removes personal locks, signs off the permit and asks the control centre to restore the unit.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 (isolation, verification, personal locks, group control) and the company permit-to-work procedure

evidence.note: Retest rate estimated.

steps.name: Travel back to shop
steps.description: The crew drives back to the area shop or on to the next site; as with the outbound trip, the minutes are this order's share of a shared trip.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Record work and hours in ERP
steps.description: The lead operator-maintainer enters actual hours, failure and cause codes, parts used and readings on the work order, and the crew's time goes into the time and attendance system for payroll.

evidence.note: Error rate estimated from typical work order data quality.

steps.name: Supervisor reviews and closes order
steps.description: The supervisor checks the work order record for completeness, approves the hours and closes the order, raising a follow-up order for defects found and flagging repeat failures for the reliability engineers.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Report incident
steps.description: After first aid or making the site safe, the crew lead enters the injury, near miss or equipment damage in the incident management system and notifies the supervisor and safety advisor, then the job resumes or is re-planned.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act and Code incident reporting duties and the company incident standard

evidence.note: Incident rate per work order estimated.

exceptions.name: Specialist crew and unit outage
exceptions.description: A major repair waits months for a specialist crew and a low-flow outage window.

exceptions.name: Parts not in stock
exceptions.description: Parts must be bought and the job waits for delivery.

exceptions.name: Urgent repair
exceptions.description: A fault that threatens a unit, gate or safety goes straight to a crew without planning.

exceptions.name: Failed test
exceptions.description: The equipment fails its return-to-service test and the crew repeats the repair.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from order release or request to closure
benchmarks.population: Hydro maintenance work orders at a multi-site generator

evidence.note: Estimate: most preventive orders are released two to four weeks before they are due and closed a week after the work; specialist jobs take months. No public benchmark found.

pain_points.description: Long drives to remote mountain and foothill plants eat crew time, so jobs are bundled by site and wait for the next trip.

evidence.note: Estimate from plant locations in s6.

pain_points.description: Major repairs wait months for a specialist crew shared with the thermal fleet and for a low-flow outage window.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Work order records are completed days later and often lack failure codes, which weakens reliability analysis.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: Hydro Generation Operator I (Calgary) job posting
sources.supports: Operators in the Calgary Hydro System Control Centre remotely monitor and operate the hydro fleet through SCADA on rotating 12-hour day and night shifts; execute AESO dispatches, ancillary services directives and voltage instructions and monitor AGC; manage reservoirs, forebays, canals and river flows within operating constraints; acknowledge and respond to alarms; coordinate switching, isolations, equipment status and after-hours response with site operations, maintenance and Hydro Scheduling; keep electronic operating logs and shift handovers. Posted November 2026, after the reference period.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2021 (Exhibit 13.1 to Form 40-F)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Alberta hydro facilities: Bow River system 11 plants (338 MW: Barrier, Bearspaw, Cascade, Ghost, Horseshoe, Interlakes, Kananaskis, Pocaterra, Rundle, Spray, Three Sisters), North Saskatchewan system 2 plants (Bighorn 120 MW, Brazeau 355 MW), Oldman system 4 small plants (21 MW); merchant sale into the Alberta spot market after PPA expiry; value from capacity, energy and ancillary services; Belly River operates April to October.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Code, Part 15: Managing the control of hazardous energy
sources.supports: Part 15 sections on isolation of machinery and equipment (s. 212), verifying isolation (s. 213), assigning personal locks (s. 214), securing by individual workers (s. 214.1) and securing by group control procedures (s. 215).

sources.title: Asset management strategies: HEPs move from reactive to proactive O&M practices
sources.supports: Hydro O&M practice: approved maintenance schedules following manufacturer guidance; annual work on underwater turbine parts; periodic inspections of water conductor systems; generator insulation and winding tests; protection system testing; vibration monitoring; move from reactive and fixed-interval maintenance to condition-based work.

assumptions: The organisation file has no hydro maintenance planner; supervisors plan and schedule, which is common in small hydro groups. A planner role would shorten the planning backlog.
Touch minutes for crew work are person-minutes for the whole crew; travel is the order's share of a trip that serves several orders.

The process map triggers this process from operations, stores, specialist crews and dam safety, but preventive orders from maintenance plans (about 62 percent) are not linked; they are shown here as coming from eng-reliability-analysis (maintenance_strategy). Issued parts are treated as an input, not a trigger.

Hands-on time is about 10 to 11 hours per order on average, which at 550 orders a month implies about 45 FTE against about 40 stated and 56 operator-maintainers and electricians in the organisation file.
